notes: Direct translation. The two rl2:Privilege clauses become permissions with rule-level assignees (an RL2 Set has no grantee); the rl2:and becomes two conjunctive constraints. The independent ex:notifyDuty becomes a root odrl:obligation whose constraint is its applicability guard. The state paths state.schemaChange.breaking and state.schemaChange.noticePeriodElapsed are flattened to two stateSource properties. RL2 has no stated conflict strategy (it is configuration); odrl:prohibit is chosen and no prohibition exists. The obligation's constraint reads a state operand, so it is a guard (due2-workflows.md §5.2): ex:notifyDuty is in force for a request that one of the policy's permissions matches, constraints aside, when the change is breaking. Its status is then reported (§6.1), which reproduces RL2's status-map entry — Active for a breaking change (scenarios 2 and 3: outstanding) — while it still plays no part in the deployChange decision under violations = ignore. A request for ex:notifyConsumers itself matches no rule of the policy, so the obligation is not in force there: an obligation is not matched by its own action (§5.2), in line with RL2's statement that no obligate atom arises from the action. Monitoring outside any request remains open (§9 #4) but no scenario needs it. Scenarios 4 and 5 are added. Scenario 4 shows a deliberate imprecision: the two permissions test the same fact with complementary values, so every actual value of ex:changeIsBreaking permits, yet due2 completes findings per atom and reports Indeterminate.

expected.why: ex:compatibleChangePrivilege applies (breaking = false). ex:breakingChangePrivilege is F: its breaking test is F, and F ∧ U = F masks the absent notice fact. The ready candidate gives Permit. Both permissions match the request, but the obligation's guard (breaking = true) is F, so ex:notifyDuty is not in force.

scenarios.name: breaking change after the notice period

expected.why: ex:breakingChangePrivilege applies (both constraints T) and has no duties; ex:compatibleChangePrivilege is F. Ready candidate, no prohibition: Permit. The permissions match and the guard is T, so ex:notifyDuty is in force; no ex:notifyConsumers witness by ex:Provider, so it is outstanding (RL2: Active).

scenarios.name: breaking change inside the notice period

expected.why: ex:compatibleChangePrivilege is F (breaking = true) and ex:breakingChangePrivilege is F (notice not elapsed). No candidate, no prohibition. The permissions still match (constraints aside) and the guard is T, so ex:notifyDuty is in force and outstanding (RL2: Active).

Both permissions are U (their breaking test is U; the notice test is T). Completions are per finding: both T gives Permit, both F gives NotApplicable, so the verdict is not invariant — even though either value of the shared fact would permit. The obligation's guard is U, so it is in force with finding U and reported unknown.

scenarios.name: request to notify consumers of a breaking change

expected.why: No permission or prohibition covers ex:notifyConsumers (ex:notifyConsumers ⊑ ex:deployChange is F). An obligation is in force only when a rule of its policy matches the request, never through its own action (§5.2), so ex:notifyDuty is not in force despite breaking = true. Nothing applies.
